title: Full research pass review of the latin early lane, 2026-10-19
semantics: Project-created review metadata. Versions include witnesses, components, translations and unresolved leads; their count is not a count of substantive revisions. Acquisition does not establish transcription, collation, normative revision or local reception. No ancestry is asserted.

rejected_by_review.reason: Triage outcome is exclusion, not a candidate: Warren 1881, p. 194 (the packet's own source) says that neither the indulgenced Gregorian orations nor any other devotion in the Liber Hymnorum has a necessary Eucharistic connection, and the packet itself records no Eucharistic order. A Gospel or hymn book is not admitted to a Eucharistic inventory without a Eucharistic component. The book and its unreconciled RIA/TCD shelfmark are kept as a scope-exclusion note in remaining_bounded_gaps, so the lead is not lost.

Duplicate identity. The baseline candidate haymo-curial-ordinal is the same component: 'Franciscan Ordo Missalis associated with Haymo of Faversham'. It already separates it from the Indutus (van Dijk, Sources II 3-14), cites O'Carroll 1979 pp. 82-84 and carries the 1243 presentation coordinate. A second row would invent a distinction. The proposal's '1243-1244 redaction' is also not in its only cited source: O'Carroll p. 82 gives only the 1243 presentation. Map the version to existing_candidate_ids ['haymo-curial-ordinal'] instead of adding a record.

uses.label: Roman libelli: Sacramentarium Veronense ('Leonianum') and Leonine-form fragments
uses.finding: Verona LXXXV (80) is a compilation of older Roman libelli copied in the later sixth century (ELMSS 866: VI²) with a separately dated seventh-century liturgical continuation; Stuttgart Cod. fragm. 100A (ELMSS 1862) is a separate seventh-century fragment of Leonine form.
uses.limit: Copy date is not the date of the libelli; no papal authorship or universal Roman book is inferred. Feltoe 1896 is the canonical edition; no new collation.
next_sources: Verona Biblioteca Capitolare digitization of LXXXV (80)
uses.review_remaining_gap: Verona digitization; relation of the Stuttgart Leonine-form fragment to the Verona collection.

uses.label: Old Gelasian sacramentary (Vatican Reg. lat. 316 with Paris BnF lat. 7193 ff. 41–56)
uses.finding: One codex in two holdings: ELMSS 118/869 date it VIII med (726–775) and treat the Paris leaves as the detached appendix of the same book.
uses.limit: Competing datings (catalogue mid-eighth century; scholarship c. 750 or later 760s–770s) are preserved; composition strata are not dated here.
next_sources: Wilson 1894 (canonical) for text; Vatican and BnF digitizations for the detached appendix

uses.label: Frankish ('eighth-century') Gelasian sacramentaries, fragments and associated liturgical components
uses.finding: Each surviving book and fragment is kept separately: Gellone, Angoulême, Phillipps 1667, St Gall 348 and 350, Rheinau 30, and the ELMSS Gelasian fragments (Brussels, Prague, Budapest, Stockholm/Wrocław, Douce f. 1, Paris lat. 2296, Cologne, Munich, Würzburg, Münster, Karlsruhe palimpsests).
uses.limit: Archetype debate open; local compilations are not one recension and copy dates are catalogue dates. 307 Gamber-index Mass-lead rows are not yet deduplicated against these.

individual holding-library records for each ELMSS fragment
uses.review_remaining_gap: 307 USUARIUM Gamber-index Mass-lead rows not deduplicated (they include already-recorded books, e.g. row 101 = Stowe); Moreton's Eighth-Century Gelasian not read.
